title: Design a video streaming service
prompt: Build a video-on-demand platform (think Netflix or YouTube playback). The dominant forcing constraint is byte-delivery: a single 4K title is tens of gigabytes, traffic is wildly geo-distributed, and the same popular segments are requested millions of times. The vast majority of those bytes must NEVER touch your origin. Draw how a viewer discovers a title (control plane: catalog, metadata, playback URLs) and how the actual video segments are delivered at scale through edge caching. Show the path from the viewer to a CDN for segments, the entry/API tier and control-plane service, and the metadata/catalog datastore behind it.

criteria.label: Playback starts from a viewer/client
criteria.metWhy: Good — the flow begins at the viewer requesting a title.
criteria.why: Add a User/Client node to represent the viewer who plays video.

criteria.label: Video segments are delivered from a CDN edge
criteria.metWhy: Excellent — a CDN absorbs the byte-delivery load so most segments never hit origin.
criteria.why: This is VOD: most bytes must be served from the edge. Add a CDN to deliver video segments close to viewers.

criteria.label: Viewer pulls segments through the CDN
criteria.metWhy: Segment traffic flows over the CDN edge — origin is spared the bulk of the bytes.
criteria.why: Connect the viewer (or the service/API issuing playback URLs) to the CDN so segment bytes travel the edge path, not your origin.

criteria.label: An API Gateway or load balancer fronts the control plane
criteria.metWhy: Good — a clear entry point routes control-plane requests (discovery, playback URL issuance).
criteria.why: Add an API Gateway or Load Balancer as the entry point for control-plane calls (browse, search, get playback URL).

criteria.label: A control-plane service handles catalog & playback logic
criteria.metWhy: Good — a service owns discovery, manifest assembly, and playback-URL issuance.
criteria.why: Add a Server/Service for the control plane (catalog lookups, manifest/playlist assembly, signed URL issuance).

criteria.label: Catalog & video metadata kept in a durable datastore
criteria.metWhy: Durable source of truth for titles, metadata, and segment manifests.
criteria.why: Add a Database to store the catalog and video metadata (titles, encodings, manifest references).

criteria.label: Service reads catalog from the datastore
criteria.metWhy: Control plane resolves titles and playback metadata from the durable store.
criteria.why: Connect the control-plane service to the Database so it can resolve catalog entries and playback metadata.

criteria.label: Hot catalog/metadata served from a cache
criteria.metWhy: Nice — a cache absorbs read-skew on popular titles and manifests.
criteria.why: Catalog reads are heavily skewed toward popular titles. Add a Cache to keep hot metadata/manifests off the database.
